projects.name: Minicontainer
projects.description: A minimal container runtime in Go implementing Linux namespaces and cgroups v2. An exploration of the isolation and resource controls underneath containers.

projects.name: modelGauge
projects.description:
modelGauge is a Go-based benchmarking tool built to help developers assess whether a GGUF language model fits a Linux deployment’s performance and resource budget. It makes model comparisons repeatable by running the same YAML-defined workloads across models, thread counts, context sizes, and concurrency levels.

Its architecture separates orchestration from inference: a host CLI communicates over a foreground HTTP stream with a controller inside a Lima-managed k3s control VM, which also hosts Prometheus and Grafana. The controller dispatches work through restricted, host-key-pinned SSH to a separate Linux benchmark VM, where a temporary supervised worker runs llama-bench and llama-server sequentially, without requiring Kubernetes or a persistent agent on the benchmark node.

Experiments capture prompt-processing and generation throughput, time to first token, latency percentiles, streaming behavior, and process and node resource consumption. Serving workloads explore sustained traffic, bursts, cache reuse, output validation, and cancellation to expose practical deployment tradeoffs.

Live dashboards follow each run through warmup, measurement, and cooldown; completed results persist as files, with JSON/CSV exports and optional raw evidence supporting later comparison and informed deployment decisions.

projects.name: Document Processing Agent Service
projects.description:
An asynchronous document analysis service that turns document URLs into structured summaries, extracted information, and classifications using LLMs. Built to explore reliable AI service design, it separates request handling from long-running analysis: FastAPI accepts jobs, Redis and RQ queue them for a background worker, and PostgreSQL persists job states, audit events, and JSONB results.

The worker downloads documents, parses PDF text with pdfplumber, calls models through LiteLLM, and validates JSON responses against Pydantic schemas before saving the output. Clients poll for progress and results while database-backed SHA-256 idempotency keys prevent duplicate submissions from creating repeated work.

Reliability features include exponential-backoff retries for model timeouts and rate limits, explicit failure states, document-size limits, and per-job token budgets.

Structured JSON logs carry correlation IDs from the API through the queue to the worker, while shared Redis-backed metrics expose completion rates, failures, token usage, and latency. Docker Compose runs the API and worker from one shared image alongside Redis and PostgreSQL, with unit, integration, and Locust load tests supporting verification.

blogs.title: I Wanted to Know What My Old MacBook Air Could Do with AI, So I Built ModelGauge
blogs.description: An old MacBook Air and a small tool for asking the same questions of your own hardware.

highlights.title: GitOps & deployments
highlights.text: Implemented an ArgoCD rollout for Dev/UAT, replacing Jenkins deployment jobs with declarative manifests and cutting mean deployment time from 30 minutes to under 5 minutes.

highlights.title: Build performance
highlights.text: Halved main-repository build times from 60 to 30 minutes with Develocity Build Cache and Test Distribution, saving 200+ engineering hours per month across 30+ developers.

highlights.title: Logging modernization
highlights.text: Evaluated a migration from Logstash to Fluent Bit through a proof of concept: analyzed logs and resource metrics, tested multiple configurations, and documented findings to guide migration planning.

highlights.title: Security hardening
highlights.text: Remediated 50+ high and critical CVEs identified by Black Duck and Prisma through dependency upgrades and code fixes, bringing the backlog close to zero.

highlights.title: CI quality
highlights.text: Hardened CI across 30+ repositories with required checks, reproducible builds, and signed artifacts, standardizing release pipelines across the organization.

highlights.title: Artifactory management
highlights.text: Diagnosed an ineffective cleanup policy, tested retention parameters with JFrog CLI dry runs, and revised automated cleanup, reducing repository usage from 96% to 30%.

highlights.title: Repository migration
highlights.text: Managed the migration of 70+ repositories from Bitbucket to GitHub. Remediated live and historical secrets, preserved workflows and permissions, validated pipeline integrations, and wrote migration runbooks and onboarding documentation.

highlights.title: Prompt-Lint
highlights.text: Built a GitHub Action treating LLM prompts as code. Four layers of static and LLM analysis block secret leaks, PII, and prompt-injection patterns at pull-request time in under 30 seconds.

openSource.name: Lima VM
openSource.description: A WSL2-style Linux VM runtime. Contributed seven merged pull requests improving guest-agent networking, storage robustness, QEMU compatibility, and CLI usability.

openSource.name: Zulip
openSource.description: An open-source team chat application organized around topic-based conversations. Contributed eight merged pull requests improving the web interface and settings validation, including rejecting duplicate custom-profile options, clarifying bot deactivation and ownership controls, refining stream settings and dark-mode styling, fixing unread markers and poll-title alignment, and adding a Busy status option.

bio.text: I’m a DevOps and Platform Engineer based in Bengaluru, India. At Amadeus Labs, I work on making development platforms faster, simpler, and more reliable, so that engineers spend their time shipping 🚀 instead of fighting their tooling. Kubernetes, CI/CD, GitOps, and observability are my everyday toolkit, and I like a pipeline that’s boring in the best possible way.

My curiosity doesn’t clock out at 6 PM. I build side projects, break and rebuild things on my homelab just to see what happens, and contribute to open source 💜. Building complex systems is my favorite rabbit hole, and I’ve never come back from one empty-handed.

When I’m not debugging, you’ll find me with a good book 📚, on a football pitch ⚽, or doing laps in a pool 🏊. I also travel ✈️ whenever I can, because the best ideas tend to show up somewhere between a train window and a new city.
This is my little corner of the web for the things I build, the moments I collect, and the books I read. Stick around 😄
